subject: Module dependency graph & CI mitigations for private deployment
messages:
From: Julia Wang <julia.wang@acme.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: acme-cloud-ops@acme.com
Date: 2027-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Module dependency graph + CI mitigations for private deployment

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the quick intro last week. Our infra team is lining up the on-prem pilot for Redwood Private and we need a clearer picture of the Terraform/Helm/Ansible module dependency surface and the practical CI gates you recommend before we grant access to our staging cluster.

Specifically we need: 
- A module-level dependency graph that shows ordering and which modules require manual approval (networking, KMS, registry).
- Concrete CI mitigations for air-gapped or restricted egress environments (how images are promoted, image signing verification, offline artifact handling).
- Any known preflight checks or smoke tests you expect customers to run before issuing prod credentials.

Can you share a draft by EOD Mar 3? Our security reviewers are asking for this to sign off on the onboarding runbook.

Julia Wang
Sr. Cloud Engineer, Acme Financials
julia.wang@acme.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Module dependency graph + CI mitigations for private deployment

Julia — thanks for the clear ask. We're on it.

Attached are two artifacts to kick off the conversation: module-deps-v0.dot (graph) and ci-mitigations-v0.md (draft mitigation checklist). Highlights:
- We call out explicit ordering: network -> core infra (vault/kms, dns) -> registry -> control-plane -> serving pools.
- For private deployments we recommend a registry mirror + signed-image verification step in CI; see section 2.
- Ansible playbooks should be idempotent but run with a read-only dry-run in CI before any apply stage.

Proposed next step: 30-minute sync (Mar 3, 10:00 PT). I added Karthik and Marissa — Karthik will validate module ordering and edge cases for terraform/helm hooks; Marissa will own CI job templates.

If that time doesn't work, let us know.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Principal Infrastructure PM, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

Attachments: module-deps-v0.dot (graph), ci-mitigations-v0.md (draft)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Julia Wang <julia.wang@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-02T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Module dependency graph + CI mitigations for private deployment

Quick technical notes after an initial pass on the dot graph and draft: 

- Terraform ordering: we should split networking into two modules: infra-network (VLANs/physical routing) and service-segmentation (security policies). The latter depends on infra-network and should be gateable.
- Helm: avoid post-install hooks that mutate cluster-level CRDs during initial bootstrap; prefer a separate post-bootstrap job triggered after canary create.
- Ansible: ensure playbooks include a simple locking mechanism (e.g., consul/etcd lease or file lock) so concurrent runs from different CI workers don't step on each other in an on-prem environment.
- Registry handling: recommend a pull-through cache for air-gapped sites + a signed-image verification stage in CI (cosign). CI should fail fast if image verification fails.
- CI job matrix: add preflight jobs that run a short terraform plan + helm template + ansible --check against a small, isolated staging namespace. I sketched a ci-job-matrix.yaml (attached) showing coverage and estimated runtimes.

I'm flagging two potential blockers for Acme's environment: image promotion (if you require signed-by KMS keys stored in an HSM) and outbound webhook callbacks for test harnesses. If either is disallowed, we should document fallback patterns.

Karthik
Head of Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
(karthik.iyer@redwood.ai)

Attachments: ci-job-matrix.yaml

From: Julia Wang <julia.wang@acme.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: acme-cloud-ops@acme.com
Date: 2027-03-03T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Module dependency graph + CI mitigations for private deployment

Thanks — meeting went well and the artifacts are helpful. A couple of security notes from our reviewers:

- We need explicit verification that KMS key material never leaves our HSM and that any signing is verified with a local key.
- Audit log retention: we require 13 months for all infra actions; will you be able to configure a separate log sink for customer-managed storage?
- No outbound callbacks to vendor-managed endpoints are allowed from our staging environment. Any callback-based smoke tests will need a local stub or an offline acceptance path.

I've uploaded our questionnaire for reference: https://acme.com/secure/questionnaire/ACME-1234

We can accept the current draft if Redwood updates the CI mitigations to: (1) support cosign with local KMS signing (HSM-friendly flow), (2) include an audit-log sink template, and (3) remove outbound callback dependencies or document a stub strategy.

Julia

(attachment: none)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Wang <julia.wang@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-04T16:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Module dependency graph + CI mitigations for private deployment

Julia — thanks for the meeting notes and the questionnaire link. Action items from Redwood side: 

1) Update ci-mitigations to document HSM-friendly cosign flow + local key verification (deliverable: ci-mitigations-v1.md).
2) Add a log-sink template for customer-managed retention (deliverable: log-sink-template.yaml).
3) Provide a no-callback CI path: local stub harness + acceptance job (deliverable: ci-job-matrix-no-callback.yaml).
4) Mark service-segmentation module as manual-approval gate in the terraform plan and add a preflight smoke job that runs terraform plan + helm template + ansible --check (deliverable: module-deps-v1.dot).

We will push these updates to the shared drive and ping you when ready (ETA: EOD Mar 7). If that timeline is tight on your end, tell us and we'll prioritize the HSM/cosign flow first.

Marissa — can you pick up the CI job templates and CI-no-callback path? Karthik — please review the module gate wording and confirm the preflight smoke job runtime estimate.

If acme approves these items after our update, we can schedule the staging pilot kickoff.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Principal Infrastructure PM, Redwood Inference

Attachments: module-deps-v1.dot (updated), ci-mitigations-v1.md (updated), log-sink-template.yaml
